key_insight: SwimBird enables a hybrid autoregressive MLLM to dynamically switch between text-based Chain-of-Thought and continuous "visual thoughts," retaining strong logical text reasoning while improving vision-intensive performance.
problem_solved: Most MLLMs either rely on textual CoT (weak on vision-heavy tasks) or inject fixed visual hidden states (which hurt text reasoning). SwimBird solves the trade-off by letting the model choose the appropriate reasoning mode per query, avoiding cross-modal interference.
method: Introduce a switchable reasoning mechanism that toggles between textual CoT and injected continuous visual states during autoregressive decoding.
Use a lightweight controller/policy and conditioning signals (special tokens or gating) so the model selects the optimal mode per input rather than using a fixed strategy.
Train with multimodal supervision and regularization to preserve textual logical capabilities while enabling expressive visual representations when needed.
impact: Practitioners get a single MLLM that handles both logic-heavy text queries and vision-intensive tasks without sacrificing one for the other, simplifying deployment and improving robustness across multimodal benchmarks.

paper_title: SwimBird: Eliciting Switchable Reasoning Mode in Hybrid Autoregressive MLLMs
paper_authors: Jintao Tong, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Xiaojun Tang, Kunyu Shi
